tools.name: load_tool
tools.description: Lazy tools (MCP and extension tools only; native tools are always in your tool list) are not in your tool list. With no arguments, list them (name and one-line summary). With names, describe lazy tools: each one's name, id, description and inputSchema. With run and arguments, run one lazy tool by its exact name or mcp:<server>:<tool>; arguments are its arguments as its inputSchema says. With runs, run several lazy tools in one call: a list of {run, arguments}, at most tools.lazy_load_max, run together when none can change state and one after another otherwise; the results come back in the order sent, each under a heading naming its run. A lazy tool is never called by its own name: a direct call is refused. names, run (with arguments) and runs cannot be combined.

names.description: Describe lazy tools: their tool names or patterns, in one call: a tool name, mcp:<server>:<tool>, mcp:<server>:* or * (every lazy tool). Returns each tool's name, id, description and inputSchema. Omit names, run and runs to list the lazy tools. The total of matched tools is limited by the profile's tools.lazy_load_max. Not together with run or runs.

run.description: Run one lazy tool: its exact tool name or mcp:<server>:<tool>, no pattern. Give its arguments in arguments, as its inputSchema says (see names). Not together with names or runs.

arguments.description: The arguments of the tool named in run. Defaults to {}. Used only with run.

runs.description: Run several lazy tools in one call: each item is run (the exact tool name or mcp:<server>:<tool>, no pattern) and arguments (as that tool's inputSchema says, default {}). At most tools.lazy_load_max items. Tools that change nothing run together; if any of them can change state they run one after another in this order. The results come back in this order, each under a heading naming its run; one failing run does not stop the others. Not together with names, run or arguments.
